title: Make every spelling of a label one label

blocks.text: The issue tracker's label filter lists `regression` three times: people typed `Regression`, ` regression` and `REGRESSION `, and each became its own label. The audit log has the same problem: it shows labels with the spacing and case they were typed with.
`Labels.Label` is a record. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/Labels.java`:

items: `normalize(...)`: the typed name without surrounding spaces, in lower case;
the record `Label`, so that every spelling of a label is one label: the same name, the same entry in a set, and the same text in the log.

cases.says: a label's name() is the typed name trimmed and in lower case
labels typed with different spacing or case are equal and count once in a set
a label prints the same normalised name that name() returns

origin.section: A Record's Accessor Is name(), and Overriding It Doesn't Change equals

concepts: A record's generated equals, hashCode and toString read the fields, not the accessors, so a value normalised in an overridden accessor makes equal-looking records unequal; normalising in the compact constructor keeps them consistent.
